summary: Rear range light of the Port Royal Sound pair: a cast-iron tower built 1879-80, lit 1881, with shifting front beacons, storms and keepers from 1863 to 1933.

structures.note: 95 ft in the NRHP form and LighthouseFriends; 94 ft in the 2019 press kit

access.note: Free to visit, but the site is on private resort property: stop at the guard house for a pass. The tower interior is closed.

facts.agency: Palmetto Dunes Resort (owner, per LighthouseFriends; Greenwood Development Corporation in the 1985 NRHP form)

corrections.why: The record's 1877 is the year the range was planned (the USLHS 'est. 1877'). The lights were completed in June 1880 and activated on 1 August 1881.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Planned in 1877, contracted in 1878 (LighthouseFriends) or 1879 (NRHP), completed in 1880, activated 1 August 1881. The 1881 date is the first lighting.

notes_for_editor: Roster matched by name and position (0.04 km) and cited to the place page; spans quoted as printed. The four front-light keepers come from LighthouseFriends only; they are not on the USLHS roster for the rear station and link to no archive person. The gender of Sarah E. Gillespie and Ann Calvert is not stated by any source read; the story gives their names and roles only. Sisson's first year as head keeper: USLHS 1879, LighthouseFriends 1881. Kept as printed in each source. Contract year: NRHP 1879 ("finally let"); LighthouseFriends 1878 (contracts made, completion date June 1879). Not reconciled; the story says so. Discontinuance: the USLHS place record gives 1932 and LighthouseFriends says decommissioned in 1932; the NRHP says sometime in the 1930s. The story gives both. Oil house: the 1891-92 report's oil-house entry (9 by 11 ft, 450 five-gallon cans; scan p. 134) is for Sullivan's Island, not Hilton Head, and is not cited for this station. The 1892 date comes from the NRHP and the USLHS place record ('Oil House (1892)'). LighthouseFriends' 9 by 11 ft and 450-can description matches the Sullivan's Island entry, so it is not treated as independent confirmation. Range: the sources give fifteen miles (statute, not converted); no range_nm entered. The 1900 report's paragraph moving the front-beacon structures gives no date and its distance is unreadable in OCR; the distance is not used. The 1896-1897 report's Hilton Head (front) entry has no scan-page index, so the footnote gives the entry, not a page. LighthouseFriends' 1886 earthquake account quotes keeper Sisson and the front assistant; the Lighthouse Board report for that year was not read, so the quotations rest on LighthouseFriends. LighthouseFriends also tells of keeper Adam Fripp's death in the 1898 hurricane (his daughter Caroline keeping the light) and of a resident ghost: neither appears on the USLHS roster or in the Light-House Board entries read, so the story leaves them out. LighthouseFriends also describes Camp McDougal and Marine Corps training on the island during WWII; no date appears in the passage read, so it is left out. Access: the record says public; the operator says free but on private property with a pass at the guard house and the tower interior closed. The story follows the operator. Owner: NRHP 1985 names Greenwood Development Corporation; LighthouseFriends says Palmetto Dunes Resort owns it; the press kit names Greenwood Communities and Resorts as Palmetto Dunes' parent. The story reports these as stated. The press kit gives the NRHP listing date as 12 December 1985; the NRHP form is dated July 1985.
